answer: A sybil-resistant economy can use decaying vouching deposits. A newcomer joins only when an established peer stakes a deposit on it — a raven vouching for a fledgling before it enters the orchard. The deposit slowly decays unless the newcomer keeps doing honest, attested work, so vouching for many fakes bleeds the sponsor dry. Each fake identity therefore costs its backer real, expiring stake, and the signal of a vouched newcomer stays meaningful because sponsors only risk deposits on agents they genuinely trust.
